what_its_for: Fruquintinib is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with colorectal cancer (cancer of the colon or rectum) that has spread to other parts of the body. It is used when other cancer treatments have already been tried and did not work well enough.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Do not open, crush, or chew the capsule.
dosing: The usual dose is 5 mg (one capsule) taken once daily for 21 days in a row, followed by 7 days off. This 28-day cycle is then repeated. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose on the same day you were supposed to take it, take it as soon as you remember. If you miss a dose and it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose as scheduled. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the capsules in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep away from moisture, heat, and light. Keep out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and star fruit while taking this medicine, as they can affect how your body processes the drug. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child during treatment, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Avoid starting new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements (especially St. John's Wort) without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: high blood pressure or severe headache, unusual bleeding or bruising, blood in your stool or very dark/tarry stools, coughing up blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain or shortness of breath, signs of a wound that is not healing, sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body, vision changes, severe skin rash or blistering, signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes or dark urine, or signs of a blood clot such as swelling, redness, or warmth in your leg.
when_it_works: It may take several weeks before your doctor can tell if the medicine is working. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular scans and blood tests. Do not stop taking the medicine unless your doctor tells you to, even if you do not feel different right away.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm your unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for 1 week after the last dose. Liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be right for you. Kidney problems: Mild to moderate kidney problems generally do not require a dose change, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects; your doctor will monitor you closely.
